clue.text: Hearts broken by proverbial madman in middle age? It's very traumatic!

indicators.note: a broken set of hearts has its letters knocked out of their order

parts.note: the saying 'as mad as a hatter'

indicators.note: the middle of 'age' is its one central letter, kept on its own

explanation.surface: A heartbroken person in a midlife crisis, compared to a raving lunatic, finds it all deeply upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'mad as a hatter', so HATTER is the madman; 'middle age' is read literally as the middle letter of AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shattering enough to shake the ground under you is hugely shocking and distressing, so the phrase works as an adjective.

clue.text: Swore at match to journalist below

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting the journalist below means adding that piece at the bottom end

parts.note: a Test match, as in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone cursed at a sports fixture while a reporter sat underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swore' looks like cursing, but here it means declared on oath. A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare formally, often under oath, which is the solemn sense of having sworn something.

clue.text: OK going back inside beer garden

indicators.note: going back means those letters are read from right to left
the letters sit within the run of the words 'beer garden'

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words, from 'beer' into 'garden'

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to head back into the pub garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts inside 'beer' and ends at the start of 'garden', then reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying OK signals consent, and to consent is to concur, so the verb and the interjection share a meaning.

clue.text: A fly larva burrowing into herb causes destruction

indicators.note: something burrowing into the herb ends up surrounded by it

explanation.surface: A grub tunnelling into a garden plant wrecks it.
explanation.walkthrough: A bot is the larva of the botfly, a word more familiar to crossword solvers than gardeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate wrecking of property or plans, so it names a kind of deliberate damage or ruin.

clue.text: Bleach it inside at what time?

indicators.note: the first word goes inside the phrase for asking at what time

parts.note: the question word for a time

explanation.surface: A housekeeper asks when the laundry should go into the bleach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At what time?' is a question, and the one-word question it asks is WHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleaching removes colour and makes things paler, which is exactly what whitening them does, so both are verbs of lightening.

clue.text: Attacker of Satan cunningly framing canvas

indicators.note: a frame goes around a picture, so the jumbled letters surround the next piece
cunningly suggests craft and trickery, so the letters of Satan are rearranged

parts.note: canvas is the cloth sails are made of, so a sail

explanation.surface: Satan, being devious, sets a painting's canvas in a frame, and so becomes an attacker.
explanation.walkthrough: Canvas suggests a painting inside a frame, but here it means a sail. 'Cunningly' rearranges SATAN into ASANT, and 'framing' puts SAIL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is a person who assaults or attacks someone, a synonym for attacker.

clue.text: Mood shifts around in one of 28 pieces

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the next word
shifts means changes position, so the letters of mood move

explanation.surface: Someone's mood keeps changing while they play a game with 28 pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifts' rearranges MOOD into DOMO, and 'around' puts it around IN. A standard double-six set of dominoes has 28 tiles.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is one tile of the game, and a standard double-six set contains exactly 28 tiles.

clue.text: Ideas man broadcast tackier TV in here

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so these words' letters are strewn about

parts.note: the fifteen letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A programme-maker puts out tawdrier television from this studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' pairs naturally with TV, disguising its role as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who comes up with original notions is an inventive thinker, which is what an ideas man is.

clue.text: Signature diagram of vehicle?

explanation.surface: Is someone's signature really just a drawing of a car?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical reading: a graph of an auto. The pieces are joined in reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograph is a person's own handwritten name, the usual word for a celebrity's signature.

clue.text: Scrub part of tennis court

indicators.note: only a part of the phrase that follows supplies the letters

parts.note: the end of 'tennis' plus most of 'court'

explanation.surface: Someone is told to clean one section of the tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span the join between 'tennis' and 'court'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to clean by hard rubbing, the same vigorous action as scrubbing.

clue.text: Wild otter grabbed the man in that place

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so the jumbled letters hold the next piece
wild means out of control, so the letters of otter are jumbled

parts.note: HE is the pronoun for the man

explanation.surface: A wild otter seized a man at a particular spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges OTTER into TRETO, and 'grabbed' puts HE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereto is a formal adverb meaning to that or in regard to that thing or place, used in legal wording.

clue.text: Artisan working for empress

indicators.note: working letters are put to use in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A craftsman is employed by a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working for' reads as employment; 'working' alone signals the rearrangement and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar or a female ruler of Russia, which made her an empress.

clue.text: Mention reported location

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by the sound

parts.note: to mention a source is to cite it

explanation.surface: A news item mentions where something happened.
explanation.walkthrough: CITE and SITE are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a specific place where something is or happens, a plain synonym for spot or position.

clue.text: Big gun welcomes the Spanish student with starter of Italian pasta

indicators.note: with means placed alongside, added after the rest
the gun welcomes guests in, taking them inside itself

parts.note: the learner plate on British cars

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An important figure hosts a Spanish student and serves an Italian pasta course first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big gun' looks like an important person but is literal artillery. 'Starter' sounds like a first course, apt next to pasta. L is a learner, as on British L-plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannelloni is a type of Italian pasta: large tubes stuffed with filling and baked in sauce.

clue.text: In high spirits and nubile? Let loose!

indicators.note: letters let loose are free to scatter into any order

explanation.surface: A lively young person urges everyone to let their hair down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let loose' reads as one phrase, but 'let' is fodder and only 'loose' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullient describes someone bubbling over with cheerful energy, which is being cheerful and full of enthusiasm.

clue.text: A corrupt builder neglecting finish can be picked up

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or twisted, so the letters are reworked
neglecting its finish means the last letter of the word builder is left off

explanation.surface: A dishonest builder who leaves the job unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neglecting finish' trims BUILDER to BUILDE, and 'corrupt' rearranges it as UDIBLE after A. 'Picked up' here means heard, not collected.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that is audible can be heard, and to pick up a sound is to detect it by ear.

clue.text: Gather wild lion is excluded from non-violence organisation

indicators.note: wild says the letters of lion need not appear in order
excluded from means the letters of lion are taken away from the longer phrase
organisation means arranging, so the remaining letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: A rally is held for a non-violence group, but a wild lion is kept out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisation' looks like the name of a group but signals rearranging. Take L, I, O, N out of NONVIOLENCE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To convene is to come together or assemble for a meeting, a synonym for the verb gather.

clue.text: Giving the green light to stick listener somewhere in the middle

indicators.note: the listener is placed somewhere within the word for stick

explanation.surface: Approving a plan to wedge a phone handset somewhere in the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhere' is fair because the placement is not the exact centre; EAR goes after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing a proposal means officially approving it, the same as authorising it to go ahead.

clue.text: Narcissism, for example, is linked to leaderless state of the EU

indicators.note: linked to means joined on, so the first piece is attached directly before the next
leaderless means the first letter of the country's name is dropped

parts.note: Romania is a member state of the European Union

explanation.surface: A political comment: narcissism is said to be tied to a member state of the EU that lacks a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless' drops the R from ROMANIA, leaving OMANIA, which follows EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an obsessive preoccupation with oneself, the same self-love that narcissism names.

clue.text: Desert wanderer blew Te Deum badly

indicators.note: a hymn played badly comes out wrong, its letters in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A nomad in the desert made a hash of playing a hymn on a horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert wanderer' suggests a nomad or camel, but it is a plant; the Te Deum is a Latin hymn of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbleweed is a plant that breaks off and rolls across arid land in the wind, so it roams dry country.

clue.text: May heartless son dwarf me

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word may is removed

parts.note: an elf is a small mythical being, like a dwarf

explanation.surface: A wish that an unkind son may make the speaker seem small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes the middle A out of MAY, leaving MY; S and ELF follow. 'Dwarf' looks like a verb but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Myself is the emphatic or reflexive form of the first-person pronoun, standing for the speaker, me.

clue.text: Rage about the extremity of Japanese flower arrangement

indicators.note: the rage goes about, surrounding, the chosen letter
the extremity of a word here is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about the finer points of ikebana, Japanese flower arranging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japanese flower arrangement' reads as ikebana, but 'Japanese' is only there for its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath is a ring of flowers and leaves woven together, a common decorative display of blooms.

clue.text: Make Scottish banks money

indicators.note: the banks of a word, like those of a river, are its two edges

parts.note: the first and last letters of 'Scottish'

explanation.surface: An instruction to earn cash from Scottish lenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish banks' suggests the banks that print Scottish notes; it means the outside letters. Dosh is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosh is informal British slang for cash, the same everyday funds as money.

clue.text: Sharp marinade

definitions.meaning: as in a sharp rise or climb

definitions.note: used as a verb: to soak in liquid

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp marinade' reads as a tangy sauce; each word is a separate definition, the second a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp incline is a sudden slope, and to marinade food is to soak it in liquid, both senses of the word.

clue.text: Break from ceremony involving paranormal activity

indicators.note: a ceremony involving something takes it in as part of itself

explanation.surface: Someone takes time out from a séance-like ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: ESP, extrasensory perception, is the usual crossword shorthand for mind-reading and other psychic powers.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short period of rest or relief from something difficult, a pause or interval.

clue.text: Gain new skills concerning the Orient Express, say

parts.note: as in business letters: 're' meaning about
a famous example of a railway service

explanation.surface: Someone takes a course about luxury rail travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' flags that the Orient Express is just an example of the thing wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrain is to learn a different trade or set of abilities, usually for a new job.

clue.text: Fibre intake of zany loner

indicators.note: an intake is something taken in, so the letters sit inside the phrase

parts.note: the end of 'zany' and the start of 'loner'

explanation.surface: A quirky recluse's diet is monitored for roughage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fibre intake' reads as dietary roughage, but 'intake of' is the signal and 'Fibre' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic polymer spun into threads for textiles, making it a man-made fibre.

clue.text: Orange granite construction associated with Tyneside

indicators.note: in construction, stone is cut and reassembled into a new form
one piece associated with another is set right beside it

parts.note: the region around Newcastle in North East England

explanation.surface: A building of coloured stone typical of the Newcastle area.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside, the area around Newcastle, lies in the North East of England, hence NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small citrus fruit of the orange family, so it is a kind of orange.
